research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
methodological_questions: Does offensive reorganization relative to L predict the change in PPP across absence spells, once team-season baselines and game-state controls are applied?
Is n=148 spells enough to detect the effect, given that the MDE is recorded only as 'rho' with no value?
Can the reorganization measure be built without using the same possessions that define the PPP-change outcome?
Does the association survive within-team baselines, placebo spells and matched comparators?

historical_evidence.finding: On/off identity displacement D_A: shaper absence displaces the team fingerprint more than a usage-matched non-shaper (Delta D_A=+0.115, t=6.35, p~7e-9, shaper larger in 81% of pairs). Correlation r(L,D_A)=+0.60 (shapers +0.79). Based on 908 player-seasons with >=400 possessions on and off and 96 usage-matched pairs. Outcome is identity displacement, not PPP change.

Connector absence displaces offensive identity more than usage-matched non-organizer absence (unmatched D_A 0.2020 vs 0.1021; paired dD_A +0.1151, n=96; vs terminal +0.0777, n=25). Outcome is identity displacement, not PPP change.

Play-type replacement similarity does not separate absorbed from cascading absences (mean sim ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848; Spearman(sim, -gap)=-0.19, wrong-signed). The record's verdict field is null and its failure type is B_powered_null, but the status is recorded as inconclusive.

Connector presence showed no PPP/TS/eFG shielding effect for stars (HasConn on-off PPP both-null: mean -0.041, p=0.939; median +0.528, p=0.731; n=73). TO rate rose with connectors. Lineup ORtg lift was explained by talent (p=0.51 after TALENT adjustment).
Routing possessions to each play type's best player: A5 vs A3 shrank from +0.94 pts/100 (V5) to +0.03 (V6, 520 matchups); A5b vs A5 -0.00. Model-scored, not observed outcomes.

Play-type cross-possession memory failed the decay sanity check (DRIVE lifts flat at +0.015 to +0.021 across lags). Lifts collapse under within-team baseline and reflect team-quality confounding (915,570 possessions).

Lag-1 play-type effects were real without controls but DRIVE and PNR effects disappeared with game-state controls or within-team baselines (DRIVE ctrl_p=0.0911; PNR controlled p=0.136). Sample size recorded as NOT_RECORDED.
Flat global PPP lifts for play types disappear after team-season demeaning; within-team memory is essentially none except SPOT_UP lag-1.
Descriptive tendency of players to land on engine BEST/AVOID counters in H2 trigger possessions (55 series). No outcome test; player samples of 10 to 178 possessions.
Star-initiator lineup and forced-play-type suppression gaps (for example Jokic vs MIN PPP 0.814, n=59). No placebo or matching, and later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type lag-based memory effects on PPP using large possession counts
failed_approaches.why: Flat non-decaying lifts collapsed under within-team baseline; team-quality confound. Large n gave p~0 for tiny effects (d~0.01-0.03).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Lag-1 play-type PPP effects after game-state controls
failed_approaches.why: DRIVE and PNR lag-1 effects disappeared with period, clock, margin controls and within-team baselines (recorded as artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Global play-type PPP lift as a persistent effect
failed_approaches.why: Lifts disappeared after team-season demeaning; classified as artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Connector presence as a PPP/TS shield for stars and lineup lift
failed_approaches.why: Adequately powered null (rejected); the lineup lift was confounded by talent.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Best-player routing value over baseline routing
failed_approaches.why: Effect shrank from +0.94 to +0.03 pts/100 on a larger sample (rejected, B_powered_null).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type similarity to separate absorption from cascade
failed_approaches.why: Similarity did not separate the groups and was wrong-signed; recorded as inconclusive with verdict null.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work on absence spells built a usable identity-displacement measure (D_A) and a leverage-type baseline L, and found that shaper and connector absence displaces team identity more than usage-matched absence (FAM:SF-PAP-014, FAM:SF-APPS-088).

Play-type and lineup PPP effects reported in earlier work were repeatedly reduced to artifacts or nulls once team-season baselines, game-state controls, or talent adjustments were applied (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-CHT-037, FAM:SF-APPS-073, FAM:SF-APPS-087).
Earlier work has repeatedly shown that unadjusted PPP differences are confounded by team quality and game state.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests reorganization relative to L against change in PPP. The supported records (FAM:SF-PAP-014, FAM:SF-APPS-088) use identity displacement as the outcome.
The retrieved records do not give the MDE value, the outcome definition for PPP change, or a power calculation for the 148-spell sample.
Nothing retrieved shows whether a reorganization measure built from the same possessions as the PPP outcome is leakage-free.
Nothing retrieved shows whether the 2025-26 playoff data (complete from 2026-06-21) is usable at the 2026-11-01 cutoff in this specific design.
own_inferences: Identity displacement (D_A) and PPP change are different constructs. A positive D_A-L relationship does not imply that reorganization predicts PPP change.
For n=148 spells, two-sided alpha=0.05 and power 0.80, the detectable correlation is about rho=0.23. Smaller effects would be underpowered.

The unit of analysis is probably the spell, so possessions within a spell are not independent. A possession-level test would overstate the effective sample size and would reproduce the p~0 pattern seen in FAM:SF-CHT-029.
The question's wording ('how much... predicts') suggests a regression coefficient or R-squared. Its interpretation depends on how reorganization is scaled relative to L.
uncertainties: The MDE 'rho' is recorded without a value, so the power is unknown.

The definition of L and of 'reorganization' is not given in the task. The retrieved records use L as a leave-one-out shaper measure and D_A as the displacement metric, but the exact mapping to this question is not confirmed.
Sample counts per spell and per team-season are not recorded.
The status of FAM:SF-CHT-052 (inconclusive) conflicts with its null verdict and B_powered_null failure type. This is recorded as stated and not reconciled.
Several retrieved records have sample_and_power or validation fields recorded as NOT_RECORDED.
The retrieval tool returned only one call's worth of records; no follow-up reads were made, so full family texts (for example SF-APPS-087 frequent-connector analysis) were not checked.

historical_effect.explanation: Prior work shows that identity displacement relative to L is measurable and has been tested as a supported result, but nothing retrieved tests L-relative reorganization against PPP change. Earlier PPP-based memory and connector effects were repeatedly reduced to artifacts or nulls by team and game-state adjustment. That history drove the decision toward a pre-specified test with spell-level inference, within-team baselines, placebo spells, and an outcome that is not derived from the same possessions as the predictor, rather than an exploratory possession-level analysis.

blocking_constraints.text: 148 spells gives detectable rho of about 0.23 at 80% power. The MDE value is unspecified, so the power for smaller effects is unknown.
If reorganization and PPP change are computed from the same possessions, the association may be mechanical.
Team quality, game state and talent confounded earlier PPP effects and must be controlled.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work answered the related question of whether shaper and connector absence displaces offensive identity (D_A), with supported results. It did not test whether L-relative reorganization predicts PPP change. Earlier PPP-based memory and connector claims were reduced to artifacts or nulls once team-season baselines, game-state controls, or talent adjustments were applied.

risks.text: 148 spells gives limited power for modest effects; the MDE must be computed before analysis.
Reorganization and PPP change may share possessions or be derived from the same play-by-play labels.
If L or the reorganization measure uses information from after the absence spell began, the association is inflated.
Team quality, game state (margin, period, clock) and talent drove earlier PPP artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-CHT-037, FAM:SF-APPS-087).
Reorganization may mechanically rise with absence size or usage, producing a floor effect (noted as a risk in FAM:SF-APPS-088).
Spells may be selected on extreme prior PPP or on injury timing, causing regression to the mean.
Play-type and initiator labels are noisy (FAM:SF-CHT-052 recorded label/classification limitations).
Star-specific gaps without placebo or matching were treated as artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-009).
Multiple L definitions, windows and outcomes increase false positives.
Four seasons with rule and pace changes; the playoffs differ from the regular season.
Earlier PPP-based claims in this project mostly failed, so the prior probability of a real effect is low.

design.estimand: Standardized association (regression coefficient and partial R-squared) between offensive reorganization relative to baseline L and the change in team PPP across player absence spells, after team-season baseline and game-state adjustment.
design.unit: Player absence spell (one team, one absent player, one contiguous window).
design.sample: 148 spells from the NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons (primary). Playoffs used only as a sensitivity analysis. 2025-26 regular season and playoffs are complete at the 2026-11-01 cutoff and may be included.
design.power: Compute the MDE before analysis. For n=148, alpha=0.05 two-sided, power 0.80, the detectable correlation is about rho=0.23. Report the achieved power for the primary coefficient. Treat smaller effects as untestable at this sample.
design.controls: Team-season fixed effects (within-team design). Game-state controls: score margin, period, clock. Matched comparators: usage-matched non-organizer absence (as in FAM:SF-APPS-088). Define L leave-one-out so it excludes the outcome window. Use only pre-spell information for L. Cluster standard errors by team.
design.falsification: Placebo spells (games without absence of the focal player) and shifted windows. Shuffle reorganization labels within team-season. Require the effect to vanish under the placebo and under within-team shuffling.
design.multiplicity: One pre-registered primary L definition and one primary outcome. Other L variants, windows and playoff analyses are secondary, with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the primary coefficient's 95% CI excludes zero after team-season and game-state controls, survives within-team shuffling and placebo spells, and the sign is as pre-registered. Artifact if the effect disappears under within-team baseline (as in FAM:SF-CHT-037). Rejected if the CI is tight around zero with achieved power of at least 0.80. Otherwise uncertain.
design.data_version: Data as of 2026-11-01 from the NBA stats API per-game files: play-by-play, substitution intervals, starters, matchup minutes, box score. Use 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) and playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21). Freeze the file version and record its hash before analysis.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
